subject: Hybrid visibility SKU proposal and pilot credit — BrightLabs request
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@brightlabs.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@brightlabs.ai>
Date: 2026-08-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging question — retention & dashboards pricing

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the earlier demo — BrightLabs is evaluating Redwood for our analytics UI and long-tail trace access. Our dashboards drive ~18TB/month of retained events and we run distributed traces for user journeys during peak windows. The thing blocking procurement is predictability: we need a pricing approach that avoids huge month-to-month swings during campaigns.

Can you sketch a pricing alternative that:
- Smooths cost for dashboards (we care about seat-based UX + high ingestion spikes)
- Gives an economical path for long-tail traces and keeps explorer queries performant
- Includes a short pilot and a one-time migration uplift credit (we have migration costs on our side)

If you can outline a concrete SKU mix (baseline seats + ingestion tiers + trace bundle) and any introductory concession, that would help our legal/procurement team move fast.

Appreciate quick turnaround — we’re hoping to close pilot commercials this quarter.

Best,
Alicia
Director, Platform Engineering
BrightLabs
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@brightlabs.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@brightlabs.ai>
Date: 2026-08-16T12:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hybrid visibility SKU proposal and pilot credit — BrightLabs request

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear ask and the usage numbers on the call. I put together a short hybrid proposal that targets cost predictability while keeping unit economics intact. I attached a simple pricing workbook and an initial SOW for the pilot. High level: 

Proposal summary (high level)
- Baseline: per-seat license for Advanced Dashboards (keeps UI UX predictable). Seats cover interactive usage and dashboard refreshes up to a baseline throughput.
- Ingest-backed tiers: for heavy retention we price retained ingestion in GB/month bands (slab pricing). This prevents sharp per-token swings while aligning with storage/egress cost.
- Tracing: trace runs included in a monthly trace bundle (X trace-runs per month), with pay-as-you-go overage at a stable unit rate.
- Keepalive/Burst buffer: a modest burst pool of tokens/queries that smooths short spikes; charged monthly as a fixed add-on to avoid variance.

Commercial concession
- Pilot: 3-month pilot (no seat commitment) to validate SLA/latency under your peak loads.
- Migration uplift credit: $25,000 one-time credit applied to first invoice to offset your migration effort.
- Intro 20% off list for year 1 if you convert to a 12-month committed plan within 60 days of pilot wrap.

Success criteria (suggested)
- Dashboard P95 latency < 350ms under simulated 2x peak load
- Trace query availability > 99.5% during pilot windows
- Ops cost per active user reduction target (we can share a workbook)

Next steps
1) If this shape looks good I’ll send a revised SOW and formal quote (with capped credit terms).
2) We can stand up a test workload next week — I’ll include Jordan from commercial for the final pricing stamp.

Attachments: Hybrid_SKU_Prices_v1.xlsx (workbook), SOW-draft-BrightLabs.pdf (pilot SOW).

Would you like to jump on a 30-min call tomorrow to walk the SKU workbook?

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-16T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Hybrid visibility SKU proposal and pilot credit — BrightLabs request

Jordan / Neha — forwarding BrightLabs ask and my proposed shape. Key context:
- BrightLabs runs ~18TB/month retained events and high trace volume during campaigns.
- They want predictability; procurement will push for slab + seat.

I proposed: 20% intro discount year-1, $25k pilot migration credit, 3-month pilot no-commit, and a hybrid baseline (seats + ingestion tiers + trace bundle + small burst pool).

Questions for commercial/finance:
1) Can we approve the $25k one-time credit (to be capped to migration labor only) on an LOE-based attestation?
2) Confirm we can apply 20% off standard list for first-year if they commit 12 months within 60 days of pilot.
3) Is the burst buffer charged as a fixed monthly add-on ok from margin perspective?

I’ve attached the workbook and draft SOW. If you need different phrasing for procurement I’ll iterate.

Thanks — Evelyn

> > Thanks for the earlier demo — BrightLabs is evaluating Redwood for our analytics UI and long-tail trace access.
> > Our dashboards drive ~18TB/month of retained events and we run distributed traces for user journeys during peak windows.
> > The thing blocking procurement is predictability: we need a pricing approach that avoids huge month-to-month swings during campaigns.
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-16T15:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hybrid visibility SKU proposal and pilot credit — BrightLabs request

Thanks Evelyn — looks sensible as a negotiable shape. A few commercial guardrails: 
- Approve the $25k migration credit conditional on a minimum 6-month conversion commitment or a signed PO covering pilot time plus conversion window. That reduces churn risk.
- Make the 20% intro discount limited to seat+ingest bundle (not applied to trace overage rates) and cap total discount exposure to the equivalent of 6 months at the discounted rate.
- Burst buffer as a fixed monthly add-on is fine but add an explicit cap and an auto-notify at 80% utilization.

I attached a short SLA-exception-request doc to capture the pilot SLA language we should use in the SOW. Once you and Neha confirm I’ll route this through pricing and legal for a quick quote.

Jordan
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
Attachment: SLA-exception-request.docx

Evelyn — thank you, this shape is helpful. Procurement reviewed the SOW and asks the migration credit be explicitly applied to our onboarding invoice (not to ongoing months). They’re fine with a 6-month conversion commitment to trigger the credit.

We accept the pilot and the commercial guardrails Jordan suggested. Please send a formal quote and DocuSign-ready SOW reflecting:
- $25k migration uplift credit applied to onboarding invoice
- 20% intro discount (applies to seat + ingestion slab only)
- 6-month conversion commitment terms and auto-notify threshold for burst buffer at 80%

Attached are our procurement standard terms (BrightLabs_Procurement_Terms.pdf). Once we get the DocuSign link we’ll route for signature.

Best,
Alicia
